scientific_card_excerpt.text: Claim: Assume the exact model and input-output germ of N594. If every physical node has the same unknown alpha>0, K is symmetric positive definite with K_ij<=0 for i!=j, and its off-diagonal graph is connected, then each active synchrony block B has reduced cubic coefficient alphabar_B=alpha/|B|, no physical coordinates are inactive, and |B|=alpha/alphabar_B is an integer. The one-port coefficient identifies alpha, so the exact germ determines the physical node count N=sum_B alpha/alphabar_B, even though hidden internal connections/eigenvalues can remain unidentifiable. This is a source-reported exact-data consequence, not a noisy census procedure.

2. HOMOGENEOUS IRREDUCIBLE SPD M-MATRICES HAVE NO INACTIVE NODES

Now impose the additional physical promises
  alpha_i=alpha>0 for EVERY physical node (unknown alpha is allowed),
  K_ij<=0 for i!=j, and the off-diagonal graph is connected.
K remains symmetric positive definite. Thus it is an irreducible SPD
M-matrix, using this precise sign/connectivity definition.

Claim: K^-1 e1 has every coordinate strictly positive.
Proof: choose s>lambda_max(K). Then A=sI-K is entrywise nonnegative
and its off-diagonal graph is connected. Its eigenvalues lie in (0,s),
so
  K^-1=(1/s) sum_(j=0)^infinity (A/s)^j.
Every summand is entrywise nonnegative. For each coordinate i, a path
from 1 to i makes some (A^j)_(i1)>0. Hence (K^-1)_(i1)>0.

Since W is K-invariant and K is invertible, K|_W is an invertible map
from W onto W. Consequently K^-1e1 belongs to W. W contains a strictly
positive vector. Its weighted signed-block classification therefore has
no inactive coordinates, and all signs within each block are equal.
Orienting each block positively makes them unsigned synchrony blocks.

For homogeneous alpha, their orthonormal vectors are simply
  v_b=1_(B_b)/sqrt(m_b), m_b=|B_b|.
The reduced cubic coefficients are
  alphabar_b=alpha/m_b.
The measured-node block is singleton, so alphabar_1=alpha. This alpha
is identified directly at the port as -G^3 Fh(0)/6.

  m_b=alpha/alphabar_b

source_excerpts.text:
2. WEIGHTED CUBIC REDUCTION

For the model f=-Kx-alpha*x^3 with alpha_i>0, let W be the smallest
K-invariant alpha-weighted-ternary-closed subspace containing e1.
Set D=diag(sqrt(alpha_i)) and U=D W. Since
  D(alpha*u*v*w)=(Du)*(Dv)*(Dw),
U is an ordinary ternary-closed subspace, so the classification applies.

For every block B, set Z_B=sum_(i in B)1/alpha_i and define
  v_B,i=s_i/(sqrt(alpha_i)*sqrt(Z_B)) if i belongs to B,
  v_B,i=0 otherwise.
These vectors are Euclidean orthonormal and span W. Let V have these
columns and choose their ordering/sign so the measured-node block is first.
The fact that e1 belongs to W forces coordinate 1 to be a singleton block:
a signed block with multiple members could not contain the vector e1.
Thus v_1=e1 and V^T e1=e1 in reduced coordinates.

Write x=V xi on W. Since K preserves W,
  Kbar=V^T K V is symmetric positive definite, K V=V Kbar.
For i in B,
  alpha_i (V xi)_i^3
    =s_i xi_B^3/(sqrt(alpha_i) Z_B^(3/2))
    =v_B,i xi_B^3/Z_B.
Consequently the zero-initial IO map is exactly that of
  xi_dot=-Kbar xi-alphabar*xi^3+e1 u, y=xi1,
  alphabar_B=1/Z_B>0.
The dimension is r=dim W. This is an exact invariant-subspace reduction,
not an approximation or Schur complement.

The reduced model has full closure. Otherwise a proper Kbar-invariant,
alphabar-ternary-closed subspace containing e1 would map under V to a
proper subspace of W with all its defining properties, contradicting
minimality of W. Thus the previously proved full-closure recovery theorem
applies to the reduced system.

For a homogeneous physical coefficient alpha, a block of size |B|
has reduced coefficient alpha/|B|. The heterogeneous-positive class is
therefore needed to express arbitrary reductions, even if the original
physical model was homogeneous. The effective coefficients do not
identify the individual alpha_i when blocks contain multiple nodes.

source_excerpts.text:
4. WHY THE PROMISES ARE MATERIAL

Arbitrary signed SPD connected networks may have inactive coordinates.
For alpha=1, the preceding 3-node example has the same IO as the
connected SPD 4-node matrix
  [[4,-1,-1,0],
   [-1,3.5,-1.5,1],
   [-1,-1.5,3.5,-1],
   [0,1,-1,6]].
Both preserve x2=x3; the fourth coordinate of the 4-node model remains
zero because its two driven couplings cancel. The canonical model is
the same, while N is respectively 3 and 4. Orthogonally, its active
restriction is the displayed Kbar, and its residual 2-by-2 restriction
is [[5,sqrt(2)],[sqrt(2),6]], proving SPD. The positive off-diagonal
entries violate the M-matrix promise.

Unknown heterogeneous coefficients also destroy the census, even for
irreducible M-matrices: only sum_(i in B)1/alpha_i is fixed, so different
block sizes can have the same harmonic sum. The complete physical
parameterization above describes these equivalences exactly.
